references.text: Psalm 23:1 presents the Lord as shepherd, an image that Jesus confirms and fulfills when he identifies himself as the good shepherd.
Ezekiel 34:11-12 describes God's promise to seek out and find his sheep himself, which mirrors Jesus' claim that he knows his own and is known by them.
Ezekiel 34:23-24 predicts that a single shepherd, David, will be shepherd for the people, a prophecy that Jesus fulfills when he says 'I am the shepherd'.
John 17:3 expands on the concept of 'knowing' in a relational sense, where knowing God and Jesus is the very core of eternal life, just as in John 10:14.
1 John 2:3-4 directly links knowledge of God to keeping his commandments, which resonates with the mutual knowledge between shepherd and sheep in John 10.
